Article Title: India’s first hydrogen-powered train completes over 1,200 km trials, saves 3,200 litres of diesel; onboard fuel cells generate electricity, emit only water vapour
Article Text:
File photo: Jind-Sonipat Hydrogen Train

Train generates electricity using hydrogen fuel cells

Developed indigenously by Indian Railways

Dedicated hydrogen storage facility set up at Jind

Multiple safety systems incorporated

Independent hydrogen leak detection systems

Heat, flame and smoke sensors

Automatic emergency shut-off systems

Continuous ventilation

Compliance with international safety standards

Mandatory technical validations before operations

Delhi trials planned next

India's first hydrogen-powered train has travelled more than 1,200 kilometres since it was flagged off on July 17, with Railways saying the project has already saved over 3,200 litres of diesel during trial operations between Jind and Sonipat in Haryana.According to a railway ministry press release, the successful trial runs have paved the way for the next phase of testing, with operations on the Delhi route expected to begin soon.Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the country's first hydrogen-powered train from Jind under the Centre's Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative.Unlike conventional diesel locomotives, the hydrogen train produces electricity onboard through a chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen inside fuel cells, according to the Railway Ministry.The electricity generated powers the train's motors, while water vapour is the only by-product released during the process.Because there is no combustion, the train produces no smoke or tailpipe carbon emissions, making it one of the cleanest forms of rail propulsion currently available, the ministry said.The hydrogen train has been developed as an indigenous project by Indian Railways.According to the railway ministry, the train consists of 10 passenger coaches and two Hydrogen Driving Power Cars that together generate 2,400 kW of power.The propulsion system is supported by lithium iron phosphate batteries along with hydrogen cylinders.Railways minister Ashwini Vaishnaw described the project as a landmark achievement, saying the propulsion system and related technology were developed within India.The project has also led to the establishment of Indian Railways' first dedicated hydrogen storage and refuelling facility at Jind.The railway ministry said green hydrogen is stored at pressures of up to 500 bar and dispensed at 350 bar. The facility has a storage capacity of around 3,000 kilograms of hydrogen to support regular train operations.According to the ministry, the train has been equipped with several safety features, including:The ministry said these measures are intended to ensure the safe operation of hydrogen-powered trains under Indian conditions.Following the successful operations between Jind and Sonipat, Indian Railways plans to begin trial runs on the Delhi route.According to the railway ministry, the project aims to establish an indigenous hydrogen rail ecosystem while supporting the country's transition towards zero-emission rail transport.Officials said the initiative could lay the foundation for wider deployment of hydrogen-powered trains across India in the future.
Article Summary: India's first hydrogen-powered train has travelled more than 1,200 kilometres since it was flagged off on July 17. The project has already saved over 3,200 litres of diesel during trial operations between Jind and Sonipat in Haryana. Indian Railways plans to begin trial runs on the Delhi route soon.

Article Title: FIRs against protesters to be quashed, compensation to be given & 5-point Charter: What Centre, CJP said in joint press meet
Article Text:
The joint press conference was attended by Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, along with CJP national spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka and CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das. (PTI image)

What govt said:

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the government response to the NEET paper leak was adequate? Yes, they acted swiftly No, they should have done more 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party on Saturday withdrew its protest against the irregularities in education system including NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar after the government agreed to its all its demands.In a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh and the CJP delegation, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said the decision was taken after an understanding that the terms would be implemented within the agreed-upon timeframe."Cockroach Janta Party declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith, with the understanding that the agreed-upon terms will be executed within the agreed-upon timelines," Das said."All our demands have been accepted, so we request the protesters to withdraw immediately and return home peacefully. We will inform you of our future strategy or any other issues. But we request the protesters to withdraw immediately," he added.Meanwhile, Nadda said the government had accepted the demands presented by the delegation, including that no police action would be taken against the protesters and that compensation would be provided to the families of students who died by suicide, in accordance with the rules and regulations."We had a long conversation today. They brought a written draft in which they made four points about the ongoing cases in agitation. Along with that, we discussed the other two demands: no retaliatory measures should be taken, compensation should be provided, and their five-point charter should be considered," Nadda said."We will provide them with copies of the FIRs, and no action will be taken. The second thing that has been said is that regarding compensation, the government has clearly stated that we also sympathize. We all have said that there will be compensation according to the rules and regulations. Whatever maximum will be possible will be given to them," he added.On the five-point charter presented by the CJP delegation, Nadda said the government would "think deeply" about the suggestions for reforms in the education examination system."This five-point charter, which you gave me, is related to reforms in education examinations. Regarding it, we have to say that we will think deeply about your charter for reforms in education examinations and, after talking to your delegation, we will try to do whatever we can. So these were their demands. I think the government has sympathetically considered all the demands they had made and has also accepted them," he added.The Centre's agreement came a after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned amid nationwide protests over the NEET paper leak.Pradhan said he had stepped down after considering the situation that had developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country, adding that the government had acted swiftly after irregularities in the NEET-UG examination surfaced by handing the probe to the CBI, cancelling the examination and announcing a re-test.Minutes after Pradhan's resignation, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had declared that the protest would continue until the remaining demands were met. He had sought Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of students who died by suicide following the paper leak and action against police personnel over the alleged crackdown on protesters on July 20.However, following three rounds of talks with the Centre, the CJP on Sunday announced that it was withdrawing its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar with immediate effect after the government accepted its remaining demands, while also agreeing to consider the party's five-point charter on examination reforms.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janata Party on Saturday withdrew its protest against the irregularities in education system including NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar. In a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh and the CJP delegation, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said the decision was taken after an understanding that terms would be implemented within the agreed-upon timeframe.

Article Title: CJP's win fuels call by 'E20 Janta Party' for no-ethanol option
Article Text:
Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association have announced a march to Parliament against E20 petrol on Aug 4

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think consumers should have the option to buy 100% petrol? Yes, consumers should have a choice No, the current policy is enough 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Inspired by Cockroach Janta Party's campaign over the NEET paper leak that led to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as education minister, a new outfit - E20 Janta Party - has stepped into the ring, demanding consumers be given the option of buying 100% petrol and seeking the resignation of road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari.The campaign has found support among transporters, with Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association announcing a march to Parliament against E20 petrol on August 4.The association alleged that the ethanol-blending policy has reduced fuel efficiency, increased maintenance costs and affected engine performance, particularly in older vehicles.Also Read: Ethanol blended fuel damaged vehicles of people, claims Maharashtra Congress chief E20 Janta Party, which gained more than 25,000 followers on X in a few hours Sunday, said it was not seeking subsidies, free fuel or withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol, but only demanding that consumers be given the choice to buy the fuel they want.It also demanded transparent fuel labelling so consumers knew what they were buying, publication of data on the costs, benefits and impact of fuel blends, and independent studies on mileage, engine performance, emissions and maintenance costs.Although ethanol-free 100-octane premium petrol has long been available in the country, it is sold only at select fuel stations and costs Rs 169 per litre, compared with Rs 102.12 per litre for standard E20 fuel (in Delhi).Minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi told Parliament last week that govt had not received "widespread or substantiated" complaints on ethanol-blended petrol affecting vehicle performance.
Article Summary: E20 Janta Party has stepped into the ring, demanding consumers be given the option of buying 100% petrol. The campaign has found support among transporters, with Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association announcing a march to Parliament.

Article Title: PM Modi taps UIDAI architect Nilekani for exam overhaul
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi; Nandan Nilekani

Task force to push tech for ‘clean’ system

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi announced Sunday a high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder and founding UIDAI chairman Nandan Nilekani to recommend measures for making India’s public examination system leak-proof, transparent and technology-driven.Modi said the panel would examine how technology could be used to clean up the examination process and make it more reliable. “The Nilekani committee will give suggestions on maximum use of technology for making exams clean and transparent,” he said, adding that the government would work on its recommendations to build a “fool-proof” system.The task force has been asked to suggest next-generation examination reforms, with a particular focus on technology as well as structural changes in the National Testing Agency and the wider testing framework.Besides Nilekani, who led the creation of Aadhaar as the first chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India, the multidisciplinary panel includes former ISRO chairman S Somanath, former Intelligence Bureau director Tapan Deka, IIT Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary and ex-CBSE chairperson Anita Karwal, and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.The choice of Nilekani signals an attempt to draw on his experience in building technology platforms at scale.The committee is expected to study the entire examination cycle — from question-paper preparation and transmission to centre management, candidate authentication and post-exam processing — and identify points where technology can reduce human intervention and plug security gaps.The announcement comes amid a wider government push to restore confidence in high-stakes entrance examinations after the NEET-UG paper leak. The Centre is also moving to strengthen penalties under the law against unfair means in public examinations.The latest task force follows the K Radhakrishnan committee’s recommendations on restructuring the NTA, improving governance and strengthening exam security. Several changes in staffing, operations and examination conduct have since been initiated, but the Nilekani panel will focus more sharply on a technology-led roadmap for future examinations.The political significance of the announcement is heightened by its timing. It came a day after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned, taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG crisis following weeks of student protests.Modi said those who had played with students’ futures were facing action, but stressed that the government also had to look ahead and create an examination system that was dependable, transparent and made maximum use of technology. The task force’s recommendations are expected to guide the next phase of the NTA overhaul.
Article Summary: Nandan Nilekani, Infosys co-founder, to head task force on exam reforms. Modi says panel will examine how technology could be used to clean up the examination process. Announcement comes amid a wider government push to restore confidence in high-stakes entrance examinations.

Article Title: At no point did government stop students from protesting: Nirmala Sitharaman
Article Text:
File photo: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

NEW DELHI: Government did not stop students from protesting at any point in time, while at the same time, it was gearing up to conduct the NEET re-examination in time and punish the culprits who had engaged in paper leaks, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said."Permission was given when they came, as soon as Dipke landed. We didn't try at any point in time to stop the protest at all. When things didn't go right at the first time when the exams were held and leak became public, and it had to be acted upon, soon the govt arrested those who had bought and sold the papers. It was the responsibility of the govt to arrest them and put into the judicial process... but equally important was that the re-examination happens in time, so that one whole year does not get affected," Sitharaman said on why the govt took long to respond to the students' protest.She stressed it was after the successful re-examination that education minister Dharmendra Pradhan took the "wise" decision to resign. "If he hadn't done that (the re-examination process), it would have been irresponsible of everybody in the system," she said.Besides, she said, India faced the risk of inflation from both external and internal factors. "...this year, there is El Nino. The catchment areas are not receiving adequate rains. So, water for irrigation and drinking is going to pose a challenge. So, inflation cannot be just imported. It is also our own," she said.
Article Summary: Government did not stop students from protesting at any point in time, says Nirmala Sitharaman. At the same time, it was gearing up to conduct the NEET re- examination in time and punish the culprits who had engaged in paper leaks.

Article Title: PM Modi hails youth for taking India to arenas once beyond reach
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi

NEW DELHI: From PV Sindhu 's racquet in Tokyo to a privately built rocket lifting off from Sriharikota, PM Narendra Modi Sunday used Mann Ki Baat to say young Indians were taking the country into arenas once considered beyond reach.In his monthly radio address, Modi singled out Sindhu's Japan Open triumph, the launch of Vikram-1, and India's performance at international science Olympiads as signs of a confident generation succeeding in sports, science and technology."Our youth have achieved remarkable feats in sports recently. PV Sindhu has become the first Indian to win the Japan Open title in badminton; the entire nation is proud of this achievement of hers," Modi said.Turning to space, he said Vikram-1, India's first privately developed orbital rocket, showed what young innovators could achieve when new doors were opened. Built by Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace, it placed six payloads in low-Earth orbit on July 18. "Keeping the interests of the youth in mind, we opened up the space sector to private enterprise, and today, the world is witnessing the results."He praised school students for winning 12 gold and seven silver medals across physics, chemistry, biology and mathematics Olympiads.Meanwhile, he lauded the youth as the energy behind the resolve of a developed India and said they will also be its biggest beneficiary as he held a virtual interaction with young participants of "Viksit Vibrant Village" programme. "When the youth directly connect with the country's challenges and their solutions, then the future will certainly be bright," he said.Speaking to youngsters who had visited border villages as part of a govt initiative, he said, "The more India's youth understand its border villages, the more easily they will know the country and connect with all its corners."
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi used Mann Ki Baat to say young Indians were taking the country into arenas once considered beyond reach. He singled out Sindhu's Japan Open triumph, the launch of Vikram-1, and India's performance at international science Olympiads.

Article Title: Jammu and Kashmir: Amid NH closure, Railways operates special trains to help stranded pilgrims
Article Text:
File photo: Northern Railway operates special trains in Kashmir

JAMMU: Northern Railway operated special trains between Kashmir Valley and Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra to assist tourists and pilgrims stranded due to heavy rainfall, landslides and shooting stones that disrupted traffic on Jammu-Srinagar National Highway.A Jammu Division railway spokesperson said the initiative aimed to provide a safe and reliable travel alternative amid persistent road closures.A special train operated on July 24 departed Sangaldan at 1.45 pm, halted at Banihal and Anantnag, and reached Srinagar at 4.40 pm. On its return journey, the train left Srinagar at 5 pm and arrived at Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra at 8.15 pm.Additionally, another train (74620) was extended from Sangaldan to Katra.On July 23, a special train operated between Srinagar and Katra.More than 1,500 passengers availed the special services.Senior Divisional Commercial Manager Uchit Singhal said the decision to run the special trains was taken immediately after bad weather and road closures disrupted travel. He advised passengers to check train updates through the NTES app, IRCTC website or the 139 helpline before commencing their journey.
Article Summary: Northern Railway operated special trains between Kashmir Valley and Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra to assist tourists and pilgrims stranded due to heavy rainfall, landslides and shooting stones. A Jammu Division railway spokesperson said the initiative aimed to provide a safe and reliable travel alternative amid persistent road closures. More than 1,500 passengers availed the special services.

Article Title: India saw more than 5,000 child adoptions last year, highest in a decade
Article Text:
Representative image

392 special needs kids adopted last year, increase of 25% over 2024-25

NEW DELHI: Amid challenges ranging from nearly 26,000 people waiting to adopt kids to only a limited number of children available in the most-sought-after 0-2 age group with adoption agencies, as many as 5,022 children were adopted between April 2025 and March 2026 - the highest in over a decade - as per data shared by Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) since 2015-16.According to CARA, as many as 4,603 children were adopted domestically and inter-country adoptions accounted for 419 children.The number of children adopted in 2024-25 stood at 4,515. Of all the children who are declared free for adoption and available in the adoption pool of Specialised Adoption Agencies (SAAs) across India, 80% are in the special needs category.In 2015-16, according to the CARA data, the total figure stood at 3,677, and breached the 4,000 mark in 2018-19 for the first time. It fell during the pandemic, before rising again in 2023-24 to cross 4,000 again.While very young children who come into the pool are immediately adopted by prospective adoptive parents (PAPs), the number of older and special needs children keeps adding up as they remain in the pool. The average waiting time for adoption is estimated to be about three years for infants and young children.Amid these challenges, CARA CEO Bhavna Saxena attributes the increase in adoptions to a focused strategy on following up with specialised adoption agencies and child welfare committees through CARA’s ‘identification cell’ to ensure that eligible children in the institutions are declared free for adoption without delays.According to the CARA database, of the 5,022 adoptions, 2,756 were of girls, 2,263 of boys and three were in the ‘others’ category. According to officials, the adoption of girls saw an increase of 8% over 2024-25 when 2,554 girls were adopted. That more girls figure on the adoption list compared to boys is in keeping with past trends.Officials point out that while many more prospective parents opting for the girl child reflects a change in mindset, there is also a view among organisations working on adoptions that the higher numbers have to do with the fact that more girls end up in adoption agencies and orphanages and are, therefore, available in the adoption pool.According to the CARA CEO, there is greater focus now on building awareness about special needs children so that parents who appear keen can be counselled and assisted to go for a special needs child.“We started the process of holding regional consultations last year and found that parents were getting encouraged to consider children with special needs. We will be strengthening the outreach this year,” Saxena further added.She said 392 special needs children were adopted last year, marking an increase of around 25% over 2024-25, when the number was 313. Also, adoptions by relatives and step-parents went up by 50%, from 820 to 1,231.Saxena said that to strengthen the system, 118 new child welfare committees were constituted and 52 new specialised agencies registered over past one year. As many as 266 new SAAs have been registered and activated since July 2024.
Article Summary: As many as 5,022 children were adopted between April 2025 and March 2026. 392 special needs kids adopted last year, increase of 25% over 2024-25. Of all the children who are declared free for adoption and available in the adoption pool of Specialised Adoption Agencies, 80% are in the special needs category.

Article Title: Nepal seeks India's approval for biometric national identity card as travel document
Article Text:
Nepal seeks India's approval for biometric National Identity card as travel document (ANI image)

Nepal plans to replace citizenship certificates

India reviews the proposal

The Kathmandu Post

Nepal has formally requested India's approval to recognise its biometric National Identity (NID) card as an official travel document for cross-border journeys, alongside passports and citizenship certificates.At present, Nepali citizens travelling to India, particularly by air, must carry either a valid passport or an original citizenship certificate. Indian citizens entering Nepal are required to present either a passport or an original voter identity card with a photograph.However, Nepal's National Identity card contains biometric information, including fingerprints, facial images and iris scans. The programme was launched as a pilot in Panchthar district and among government employees in 2009. So far, more than 4.5 million Nepali citizens have received the card, while nearly 20 million applications have been submitted.The request comes as Nepal gradually makes the biometric National Identity card mandatory for banking, land registration, passport issuance and access to public services, with plans to eventually replace citizenship certificates."In the long run, we will have a single identity card replacing the citizenship certificate.It is verified, authentic and technology-friendly," Tiwari said."That is why we have requested India to allow the use of the National Identity Card while travelling by both air and land routes," he added.According to senior immigration officials quoted by, an Indian Embassy delegation met officials from Nepal's Department of Immigration earlier this week to discuss the proposalThe delegation was reportedly "positive" about the initiative and informed Nepalese officials that the request had been forwarded to authorities in New Delhi for consideration."We have already forwarded the proposal to the Indian side through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs," said Ram Chandra Tiwari, Director General of the Department of Immigration.Officials from Nepal's Home Ministry also said that discussions have included creating formal mechanisms to record cross-border travel data and better manage movement between the two neighbouring countries.
Article Summary: Nepal has formally requested India's approval to recognise its biometric National Identity (NID) card as an official travel document. At present, Nepali citizens travelling to India, particularly by air, must carry either a valid passport or original citizenship certificate. Indian citizens entering Nepal are required to present either a passport or an original voter identity card with a photograph.

Article Title: Did you approve lethal force, pellet guns: Rahul Gandhi to Amit Shah; bill in Lok Sabha today
Article Text:
File photo: Rahul Gandhi

Govt won’t like to be seen as making direct concessions to Cong, say NDA circles

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi shot off a letter to Union home minister Amit Shah , demanding accountability for police's alleged high-handedness against protesters at Jantar Mantar, signalling a fiery start to the second week of the Monsoon session, as govt is set to table in Lok Sabha on Monday a bill that enhances punishment in cases of paper leaks as part of its raft of measures to respond to the protest.Opposition MPs said they will finalise their stand at their strategy meeting before parliamentary proceedings begin. LS leader of the opposition Rahul's letter to Shah gave an early indication."As home minister, did you approve the use of lethal force including pellet guns against students? If not, who did? Are the people in plainclothes seen beating students with lathis police personnel or volunteers? Youth and students, future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability," he said, noting that security forces deployed in Delhi answer ultimately to Shah.A day after education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned to pacify Cockroach Janta Party and the opposition, PM Modi said in a message to students that govt will bring to Parliament the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill as he announced a taskforce for exam reforms.With govt determined to wrest back the initiative after making several concessions over the paper leak row and Congress and its allies keen to press home their advantage, both sides will need to come to an agreement for normal business to return to Parliament after the first week’s washout.The view within BJP-led NDA circles is that govt would not like to be seen making any direct concession to Congress, and instead point to the measures it has taken in the last few days.With Modi announcing the task force, Shah said this underlines govt’s principle of constant reform to safeguard future of the new generation. “The task force will ensure that no one can ever breach the sanctity of our exam system. We will impose exemplary punishment on culprits of paper leak and ensure no one ever dares commit this crime,” he said.Govt has said paper leaks have happened in different states irrespective of political affiliations of govt of the day. “Govt has shown a big heart and underscored its sincerity. We are hopeful opposition will now allow a debate to take place. But if they continue to play politics, we’ll hit back,” a govt functionary said.In his letter, Rahul accused police of “barbaric assault” on students during their march to Parliament on July 20. Congress’s Jairam Ramesh demanded an apology from Modi, with opposition MPs Sagarika Ghose of TMC and CPM’s John Brittas echoing the charge. The latter called for a judicial panel to inquire into the assault.
Article Summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi shot off a letter to Union home minister Amit Shah demanding accountability for police's alleged high-handedness against protesters at Jantar Mantar. Opposition MPs said they will finalise their stand at their strategy meeting before parliamentary proceedings begin. govt is set to table in Lok Sabha on Monday a bill that enhances punishment in cases of paper leaks.

Article Title: 3 Indians die in workplace accidents in Gulf every week, shows MEA data
Article Text:
Most Indians in the Gulf are employed in sectors like construction, retail, warehouses and automobiles, where occupational risks are high.

Further, to ensure women’s safety, only state-run agencies have been authorised to recruit female workers holding ECR passports to the Gulf through the e-Migrate portal, the minister said.

HYDERABAD: Over 800 Indian expats died in workplace accidents between 2023 and 2025, according to MEA data. Of these, 55% occurred in Gulf countries, which recorded nearly three deaths a week on an average. The latest incident — the Qatar blast that killed 12 Indians last month — has renewed calls for scrutiny of safety lapses.According to MEA data, Saudi Arabia recorded the highest toll, with 182 deaths over the three-year period — more than one Indian worker every week — followed by UAE with 128 fatalities.A majority of suicides during the period were also reported from Gulf nations, underscoring the challenges faced by migrant workers.Telangana NRI Migrants’ Association attributed the recurring fatalities to multiple factors: inadequate use of safety equipment, poor adherence to workplace safety protocols, technical failures at industrial sites and insufficient skill and safety training.Many workers, they said, labour in temperatures exceeding 45 degrees Celsius and return to accommodations cooled to 20 degrees Celsius, exposing their bodies to temperature swings of 20-25 degrees Celsius, which can lead to serious health complications.Most Indians in the Gulf are employed in sectors like construction, retail, warehouses and automobiles, where occupational risks are high.“At times, workers neglect their own safety by failing to wear protective gear such as helmets, boots and gloves while working in hazardous industries. In several cases, they are unaware of the risks,” said Manda Bheem Reddy, vice-chairman, Telangana NRI Cell.The high number of suicides, the migrants’ welfare association said, is often driven by cramped quarters and poor-quality food, coupled with extremely hectic work schedules. “Also, workers often go without salaries for up to three months while putting in shifts of 12 hours a day. Even when wages are paid, deductions are common, adding to their str-ess,” said B M Vinod Kumar, chairman, Telangana govt’s NRI advisory committee.Many employers allegedly evade responsibility by attributing workplace deaths to “natural causes” such as heart attacks, Vinod claimed. Only a few provide compensation through insurance coverage.According to MEA, govt accords high priority to the safety and well-being of Indians abroad and there are channels to enable them to reach out to missions.Kirti Vardhan Singh, minister of state for external affairs, said in Rajya Sabha that Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendras have been set up in locations such as New Delhi, Dubai, Riyadh and Jeddah. “There are dedicated labour wings... Indian missions regularly organise open house and consular camps in remote areas to get feedback from the workers...,” she said.Further, to ensure women’s safety, only state-run agencies have been authorised to recruit female workers holding ECR passports to the Gulf through the e-Migrate portal, the minister said.
Article Summary: Over 800 Indian expats died in workplace accidents between 2023 and 2025, according to MEA data. Of these, 55% occurred in Gulf countries, which recorded nearly three deaths a week on an average. Most Indians in the Gulf are employed in sectors like construction, retail, warehouses and automobiles.

Article Title: Ethanol blended fuel damaged vehicles of people, claims Maharashtra Congress chief
Article Text:
Representative image

MUMBAI: Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal on Sunday alleged that ethanol-blended fuel has damaged vehicles of people and demanded Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari's resignation.Addressing reporters in Buldhana, Sapkal said that after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned over the NEET-UG paper leak, Gadkari should also step down over what he termed the "ethanol scam".He alleged that vehicles of ordinary motorists, who were being sold ethanol-blended petrol and diesel, have suffered extensive damage, while companies manufacturing ethanol had earned huge profits.Sapkal claimed the Centre's ethanol policy represented both "corruption" and "harassment" of citizens, and described it as a major scam.The Congress leader also urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to apologise to vehicle owners whose vehicles were allegedly damaged due to ethanol-blended fuel.The E20 ethanol-blending policy has sparked a major controversy, centring on claims of reduced vehicle mileage, potential engine wear, and alleged conflicts of interest. The government has defended the programme, ruling out any immediate plan to increase blends beyond 20 per cent and asserting that the fuel is safe, clean, and helps farmers.
Article Summary: M Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal alleged that ethanol- blended fuel has damaged vehicles of people. He demanded Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari's resignation. The Congress leader also urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to apologise to vehicle owners whose vehicles were allegedly damaged.

Article Title: ‘Responsible for brutal assault on innocent students’: After Dharmendra Pradhan, opposition turns heat on Amit Shah, seeks resignation
Article Text:
File photo: Union home minister Amit Shah

Opposition prepares to corner government in Parliament

Questions over higher education secretary appointment

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act? Strongly support Oppose 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The opposition is set to intensify its attack on the government in Parliament on Monday by demanding the resignation of Union home minister Amit Shah over the police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak, CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas said.Speaking to reporters in New Delhi on Sunday, Brittas said opposition parties would also raise the appointment of Naresh Pal Gangwar as secretary, department of higher education, when Parliament resumes.The remarks come a day after education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following a 36-day agitation led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), with the government also accepting the protesters' other key demands."Last day, Shah said the government respected the youth who led the protest. Where was that respect for the last 36 days? When students were being beaten on the streets of the national capital, and their skulls were being cracked open, where was that respect?" Brittas said."If there is even a grain of sincerity in those words, Amit Shah too should resign. Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. The home minister, who is responsible for this brutal assault on innocent students, must resign," he added.Brittas said the opposition would support any move to strengthen laws against examination-related fraud but questioned the government's decision to amend the existing legislation instead of ensuring its implementation.He noted that Parliament had enacted the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act in 2024 after the government claimed it would curb paper leaks."Now the government is only proposing amendments to that law. The problem is not the absence of legislation but the lack of political will to enforce it and the authorities' alleged compromise with vested interests," he claimed.INDIA bloc parties are planning to seek an urgent discussion in Parliament on the alleged use of excessive force against students protesting the NEET paper leak.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has written to home minister Amit Shah seeking accountability, while Trinamool Congress MP Sagarika Ghose has submitted a notice in the Rajya Sabha seeking suspension of business to discuss the issue.The opposition is expected to raise allegations regarding the use of pellet guns, the deployment of men in plain clothes during the July 20 protest, and injuries suffered by students. The government, meanwhile, is scheduled to introduce amendments to the anti-paper leak law in the Lok Sabha on Monday.The proposed Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, seeks stricter penalties for paper leaks, including imprisonment of up to 10 years and fines of up to Rs 50 lakh for individuals involved, while organised crimes related to examination fraud could attract fines of up to Rs 10 crore.Brittas also questioned the appointment of Naresh Pal Gangwar as secretary, department of higher education, alleging that the officer had previously faced accusations of irregularities in the disbursal of central government subsidies."Such an officer has now been appointed to head the department responsible for public examinations, where transparency and integrity are of utmost importance. All these issues will be raised during the discussion in Parliament," he said.He further alleged that while authorities had released details of police personnel injured during the protests, no information had been made public about injured students."The home ministry has released details of police personnel who were allegedly injured. But not a single detail has been made public about the protesters who were brutally assaulted. There is a complete veil of secrecy over their condition," Brittas claimed.He said the identities and medical condition of injured students should be disclosed so that their families and organisations willing to assist them could provide support.Separately, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut also blamed Amit Shah for the police action during the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march organised by the CJP at Jantar Mantar.Raut alleged that students were attacked and women protesters were harassed, holding the home minister responsible for the incident. He also claimed Shah was responsible for "whatever bad and undemocratic is happening in the country."The BJP rejected Raut's remarks, with Maharashtra BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban asking the Shiv Sena (UBT) leader to focus on his "already depleted party".The protests, which began on June 20 over the NEET paper leak, were called off on Saturday after the government accepted key demands of the protesters and Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down as education minister.The July 20 police action against protesters marching towards Parliament has since become a major flashpoint, with opposition parties alleging excessive use of force, including pellet guns.Delhi Police has denied using pellet guns during the protest, while the CRPF has not publicly responded to allegations involving its Rapid Action Force.
Article Summary: Opposition to intensify attack on government in Parliament on Monday. Will demand the resignation of Union home minister Amit Shah over police action. Opposition will also raise appointment of Naresh Pal Gangwar as higher education secretary. Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following 36-day agitation.

Article Title: 'Every generation of Indians qualifies as ... ': Shashi Tharoor's reply to son Ishaan's 'ban Boomers on WhatsApp' remark
Article Text:
Debate sparked by Sridhar Vembu's proposal



NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Sunday offered a witty response to his son Ishaan Tharoor's social media post calling for a ban on "boomers" using WhatsApp, adding a humorous twist to an ongoing debate over children's access to social media.The exchange began after Ishaan reacted to Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu's suggestion that India should ban young children from using social media, similar to recently approved restrictions in France."I agree young kids should not be on social media at all. But India needs to ban Boomers on WhatsApp first before it does anything else," Ishaan wrote on X.Responding to the post, Shashi Tharoor quipped, "Given our reproductive patterns, my son, unlike in the West, every generation of Indians, including yours, qualifies as [baby]Boomers!"The online exchange followed comments by Sridhar Vembu, who backed restrictions on children's use of social media after France passed legislation banning children under the age of 15 from accessing social media platforms and prohibiting mobile phone use in schools.Vembu argued that young children should spend less time on digital platforms and more time engaging in outdoor activities and reading."India should ban social media for young children too. I believe young children should read physical books, play in the dirt under the sun, and stay away from social media!" he said.His remarks triggered mixed reactions online, with some users supporting stricter controls on children's social media use, while others argued that such decisions should be left to parents rather than the government.The term "boomer", originally referring to people born between 1946 and 1964 during the post-World War II baby boom, is now commonly used online as slang for older people perceived to hold outdated views or frequently offer unsolicited advice.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor responds to his son Ishaan's social media post calling for a ban on "boomers" using WhatsApp. The exchange began after Ishaaan reacted to Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu's suggestion that India should ban young children from using social media. France passed legislation banning children under the age of 15 from accessing social media platforms.

Article Title: Ship with 4 Indians hit at Ukraine port; 2 safe, fate of 2 unknown
Article Text:
File photo: A merchant vessel carrying four Indian nationals was struck at Ukraine's Port of Odesa

Government asks sailors for detailed info on ship’s intended route

NEW DELHI: Following the killing of five Indian nationals in the Russia-Ukraine conflict in recent days, the govt warned Indians intending to undertake employment on commercial vessels operating in or transiting the conflict-affected Black Sea region to carefully assess the prevailing security risks before accepting such assignments.The advisory came hours after a merchant vessel carrying four Indians was struck at Ukraine's Odesa port. India's embassy in Ukraine said on Sunday that while two of the Indians were safe, information about the other two was awaited.The incident occurred on Saturday when MV AGN Ragnar was hit at the port of Odesa, one of Ukraine's key Black Sea ports that has frequently come under attack since the outbreak of the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The embassy said search and rescue operations were in progress and that it was in constant contact with the authorities concerned to ascertain the status of the missing crew members and provide all possible assistance.The MEA advisory said those who choose to undertake such employment should exercise utmost caution.“The security situation in and around the Black Sea and adjoining maritime areas remains highly volatile due to the ongoing conflict.Commercial vessels operating in or transiting these waters are facing significant security risks, including missile and drone attacks,” said the ministry.It added that since April 2026, there has been an increase in the number of such incidents on commercial vessels resulting in the loss of five Indian lives.Govt also asked Indian nationals to obtain comprehensive information from employers/recruitment agencies and ship operators regarding the vessel’s intended route, ports of call, security arrangements, insurance coverage and emergency response procedures.Meanwhile, urging all stakeholders to be more cautious in the light of ongoing tension across sea routes, the country’s maritime regulator DG Shipping on Friday retweeted the advisory of Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFCIOR), a 24x7 regional maritime security centre hosted by the Indian Navy.In the post on X, IFCIOR said maritime security environment across Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Aden, Bab-al-Mandab and Red Sea remained “highly volatile”, with concurrent hybrid threats, piracy activity and route-specific risks affecting commercial shipping.
Article Summary: Government asks sailors for detailed info on ship’s intended route and security arrangements. advisory came hours after a merchant vessel carrying four Indians was struck at Ukraine's Odesa port. India's embassy in Ukraine said on Sunday that while two of the Indians were safe, information about the other two was awaited.

Article Title: ‘Banned chemical’: CPCB red-flags new ‘green’ crackers
Article Text:
The Centre had asked CSIR-NEERI to develop green/low-emission fireworks with pollution reduction of more than 50% in association with fireworks manufacturers

NEW DELHI: There is no unanimity on allowing commercial production of next-generation green firecrackers in the country, with two govt organisations taking contradictory stands in Supreme Court Council of Scientific and Industrial Research - National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) has approved the new formulations, stating that they reduce pollution levels by 40-60%. In contrast, Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has objected, arguing that these crackers still contain barium nitrate - a chemical banned by the SC - and, therefore, cannot be permitted.The Centre had asked CSIR-NEERI to develop green/low-emission fireworks with pollution reduction of more than 50% in association with fireworks manufacturers. Thereafter, Tamil Nadu Fireworks and Amorces Manufacturers' Association (TANFAMA) devised new-generation fireworks formulations with reduced quantity of barium salts/nitrates in combination with other oxidisers for particulate emission reduction of more than 50%.As per the CSIR-NEERI report, emission reductions achieved for PM10 and PM2.5 were between 45% and 60%, and recommended that these formulations for light-emission fireworks, such as flowerpots, sparklers, chakkars, pencils and twinkling stars and their hybrids, may be considered for commercial production.It also approved manufacture of joined crackers, known as 'ladis', which have been banned as per the court's order. The report said there was a reduction in particulate matter (PM) emissions by approximately 30% and a reduction in solid waste generation by up to 32% for joined crackers.Responding to the CSIR-NEERI report, CPCB raised objection on how barium nitrate could be used in crackers as it was banned by the apex court and allowing their production would be in violation of the court's order. "This court, vide order dated Oct 23, 2018, has expressly banned the use of barium salts in firecrackers and, therefore, any formulation involving barium compounds, even in reduced quantities, is in contravention of the said order," the board said."The reported reduction in PM10 and PM2.5 levels has not been comparatively assessed with (i) improved low-emission crackers and (ii) green crackers formulated entirely without barium, rendering the claim incomplete and inconclusive," it further said.Caught between contradictory stands taken by two expert bodies, the ministry of environment, forest and climate change filed an affidavit bringing it to the apex court's notice and left it to the SC to take a decision on the issue. It also informed the court that the composition of new-generation firecrackers was sent to the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), which is the regulatory body for explosive substances, and it had given a no-objection certificate to the new formulation of firecrackers.
Article Summary: There is no unanimity on allowing commercial production of next-generation green firecrackers. Supreme Court Council of Scientific and Industrial Research - National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) has approved the new formulations. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has objected, arguing that these crackers still contain barium nitrate.

Article Title: Opposition to take on government in Parliament over police action against protesting student
Article Text:
File photo: Opposition camp protesting against ruling MPs outside Parliament (Picture credit: PTI)

NEW DELHI: The second week of the monsoon session of Parliament is set for a fiery start with the opposition led by the Congress set to mount its attack on the govt over the alleged police brutality against protesting students, demanding accountability and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi set the tone by writing a letter to Home minister Amit Shah on Sunday demanding accountability for the "barbaric assault" on students who were peacefully protesting on July 20.“Our students were demanding a fair and accountable education system. Instead of being heard, security forces assaulted them with indiscriminate force, including lethal weapons and tear gas. Hundreds have suffered serious injuries. Women students have been assaulted by policemen, including by deliberately targeting their private parts. Most shocking has been the use of lethal pellet guns,” Gandhi said in the letter.He went on to cite his meeting with 19 - year old student Sahil Lochab, who he said "is now in severe pain and is likely to lose an eye because he was shot with pellet guns”.Security forces deployed in Delhi answer ultimately to you, so I ask, “As Home minister, did you approve the use of lethal force including pellet guns against students? If not, who did?”“Are the people in plain clothes seen beating students with lathis police personnel or volunteers? Who authorised their deployment?,” he asked Shah.“Youth and students, the future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability. Their voices will be heard,” he added.Sharing the letter, Congress general secretary, in-charge of communications, Jairam Ramesh said in a post in Hindi on X, “The home minister must answer these crucial questions in Parliament tomorrow. The prime minister should apologise to the students."Meanwhile, the floor strategy of the opposition and its position on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 being brought by the govt will be finalised at the INDIA bloc meeting in Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge's chamber in Parliament on Monday.There is a strong view among INDIA bloc leaders that the demand for accountability and action against Delhi Police over the action against protesting students needs to be raised strongly and the responsibility of Home Minister Amit Shah needs to be underscored.Resonating the sentiment of the opposition, TMC's Rajya Sabha’s deputy leader Sagarika Ghose has submitted a notice under Rule 267 seeking suspension of the day's business in the Rajya Sabha on Monday to allow an immediate discussion on the "use of excessive force on student protestors during NEET examination protests".Ghose said the right to peaceful protest was a constitutional right, but student protesters had allegedly been subjected to "lethal and semi-lethal force" by security agencies. Her notice also raised the question as to who authorised the use of such weapons and what protocols were followed.CPI(M) MP John Brittas said,"Everyone is anxious about the functioning of Parliament! But are we not equally outraged by the blatant violation of every rule and regulation, and the ruthless use of lethal weapons against unarmed, innocent protesters? Can the Home Minister — who is directly responsible for the Delhi Police and the administration of Delhi — simply wash his hands of this shameful and shocking episode? When such brutal atrocities are unleashed in the national capital, how can responsibility not be fixed?. ""Beyond fixing responsibility, a judicial commission must be immediately constituted to inquire into this assault. We possess a mountain of evidence that conclusively proves every fundamental principle of law and regulation have been trampled upon," he added.
Article Summary: The opposition led by the Congress is set to mount its attack on the govt over the alleged police brutality against protesting students. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi set the tone by writing a letter to Home minister Amit Shah on Sunday demanding accountability for the "barbaric assault" on students.

Article Title: 'No responsibilities': Mohan Bhagwat on live-in relationships; says marriage 'instils dharma'
Article Text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Sunday described marriage as a discipline that "instils dharma", while saying that the "reality of live-in relationships can be seen all over the world.""Marriage is a discipline which instils dharma. Its alternative is live-in relationship. Modernity. What are its consequences? We don't want responsibilities but happiness. Stay together when it is wanted and part ways when not wanted. No responsibilities. What will grow with it? What is growing, look around the world," PTI quoted Bhagwat as saying.The RSS chief was addressing an event in Hyderabad.He, however, stressed that modernity was also necessary and that adapting to changing times was "part of the country's traditions."In an apparent reference to live-in relationships, Bhagwat described them as a "degradation" and "blind imitation of Western culture", while welcoming modernity.He also maintained that LGBTQ people are a part of society and should not be looked down upon.Bhagwat favoured parents following mobile phone discipline and stressed the importance of conversations among family members to address the questions of the younger generation and various family-related issues.Addressing concerns over the lifestyle choices of the younger generation, including excessive mobile phone use, he urged elders to practise what they want to see in their children."Be the change you want to see in society. Reduce your time on social media. Follow mobile discipline. We look to the government. In our tradition, the government is second; society is first. (We say) the government should make this law or that law... we can do that at our home," he said."We tell children about mobile discipline, but we are attached to mobiles. So much so that a mother gives a mobile to a child if the child is crying," Bhagwat added.He further argued that British rule made Indians believe that everything ancient was "worthless," adding that Western countries were facing problems due to an incomplete vision of various issues that India had also adopted.
Article Summary: Mohan Bhagwat: Marriage is a discipline which instils dharma. Its alternative is live-in relationship. Modernity. What are its consequences? We don't want responsibilities but happiness. Stay together when it is wanted and part ways when not wanted.

Article Title: 'Attempt to repair PM's tarnished image': Congress on high-powered exam reforms task force
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi; Jairam Ramesh

NEW DELHI: Reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's announcement of a high-powered task force on examination reforms, the Congress on Sunday termed it a "high-powered attempt" by the prime minister to "repair" his "irreparably tarnished image. ""Friends, in June 2024, after irregularities in several exams, including NEET-UG, the Modi government formed a high-level expert committee chaired by former ISRO chairman Dr K. Radhakrishnan to 'ensure the transparent, smooth, and fair conduct of examinations.' In July 2026, after irregularities once again in NEET-UG and other exams, the Modi government has formed a 'high-level task force' to focus on exam reforms," Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X shortly after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's announcement.He added that the government was yet to fully implement the 101 recommendations made by the Radhakrishnan committee."Instead, for nearly two years between 2024 and 2026, it did not even appoint a full-time director general for the National Testing Agency (NTA). Ultimately, all of this is nothing but a high-powered attempt to repair the Prime Minister's irreparably tarnished image," Ramesh said.PM Modi's announcement came amid demands for examination reforms following the NEET (UG) question paper leak controversy, which affected over 22 lakh aspirants.On Saturday, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online satirical platform, ended its indefinite sit-in at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and broader education reforms.CJP ended its agitation hours after Pradhan resigned, as student protests intensified in Delhi and other parts of the country. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi has been given additional charge of the Ministry of Education.Meanwhile, besides Nilekani, who co-founded IT giant Infosys, other members of the high-powered task force include former Isro chairman S Somanath, ex-Intelligence Bureau director Tapan Deka, IIT Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary Anita Karwal, and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.According to the prime minister, the government will implement the task force's recommendations to establish a "foolproof examination system."The panel will help revamp NTA examinations, with a focus on technology-driven improvements and structural reforms in the system, PM Modi added.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a high-powered task force on examination reforms. Congress MP Jairam Ramesh called it a "high-powered attempt" by the prime minister to "repair" his "irreparably tarnished image" PM Modi's announcement came amid demands for examination reforms following the NEET (UG) question paper leak controversy.

Article Title: From Jantar Mantar to Parliament: Govt, opposition brace for fight over NEET row, other issues
Article Text:
Monsoon session of Parliament

How protests changed the political script

Rahul raises stakes with Amit Shah attack

PM Modi's reform push takes centre stage

The battle lines for Round 2

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with the calls for accountability for police actions against protesters? Strongly agree Disagree 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The protests are over. Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned as Union education minister. A slew of reform measures have been announced. Jantar Mantar is now clear of protesters. So, is the fight against NEET-UG paper leak over? Perhaps not. While the CJP led by Abhijeet Dipke has promised to keep a close eye on developments going forward, the opposition parties have signalled that they will keep the pressure going.As the government and the opposition brace for the second week of the monsoon session from Monday, the stage has been set for the Round 2 of this confrontation.The government, armed with a slew of reform measures in the last few days, is all prepared to counter the opposition offensive. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has himself led this fightback. His video selfie messages to the youth, the latest of which on Sunday evening announced the setting up of a task force for exam reforms, is an indication that the government is reaching out directly to the students to blunt the opposition attacks.Ahead of the monsoon session, the BJP-led NDA had managed to put the opposition on the backfoot by increasing its numbers in both the Houses of Parliament with some smart political manoeuvres in West Bengal, Maharashtra and Punjab. But as the session started, the students’ protest upset all its calculations and, for the government, the first week was anything but disappointing if not out of control.While the BJP-led NDA was all geared up to fight the opposition inside Parliament, it could not assess the fact that the youth who effectively took up the opposition space outside Parliament were a bigger challenge.The late realisation perhaps powered the course correction and the government sacrificed a minister in a rare acceptance of pressure.So far so good. But the big question now is: Can the opposition sustain the pressure built up by the students’ protest? When monsoon session resumes on Monday - there could be aggression from both sides. The government, having been forced to take a step back, is likely to come back with a vengeance against a “familiar political rival” that it has on several occasions handled with ease. The opposition, meanwhile, will try to build on the momentum created by the youth protests and hope to pile pressure.Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has already set the stage for the Round 2 of the confrontation inside Parliament. Rahul has launched a direct attack on Union home minister Amit Shah, holding him personally responsible for police action and excessive use of force, including allegedly using pellet guns, against student protesters in the national capital.In a letter to Amit Shah, Rahul demanded accountability for what he termed the "barbaric assault" on peacefully protesting students and questioned whether the home minister had approved the use of "lethal force", including pellet guns, against the youth.The Congress leader alleged that hundreds of students had suffered injuries during the police action and claimed women protesters were assaulted by police personnel.Referring to 19-year-old student Sahil Lochab, whom he had met on Friday, Rahul said the student was likely to lose vision in one eye after allegedly being hit by pellets during the July 20 protest.Rahul also sought to know whether men in plainclothes seen beating students with lathis were police personnel or volunteers and who had authorised their deployment, saying "the country is demanding answers".The other opposition parties are also keen to capitalise on what is being perceived as the government’s “moment of weakness.” Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha deputy leader Ghose submitted a notice under Rule 267 seeking suspension of the day's business in the Upper House on Monday to allow an immediate discussion on what she described as the "use of excessive force on student protestors during NEET examination protests".Calling it a matter of grave national importance, Ghose said the right to peaceful protest was a constitutional right, but student protesters had allegedly been subjected to "lethal and semi-lethal force" by security agencies.Her notice also referred to reports of pellet gun injuries, "including the possible loss of vision of one student due to use of the pellet gun by the Rapid Action Force", and sought answers on who authorised the use of such weapons and what protocols were followed.Rahul’s direct attack on Amit Shah is likely to play out in the House tomorrow. The Union home minister, who was believed to be largely working behind the scenes to defuse the situation, may lead the government offensive inside Parliament.For now, BJP leaders have taken up the cudgels on his behalf. Responding to Gandhi's letter, BJP leader Mrityunjay Tiwari accused the Congress of trying to exploit the issue for political purposes rather than genuinely standing with students."They did not do anything for the youth until recently. Now, they raised their voice just to incite agitation. They do not really care about the students. However, the Modi government has ensured that no one can commit any wrongdoing when it comes to the students, who are the future of this nation," Tiwary said.BJP leader P V N Madhav also criticised Rahul, alleging that the Congress leader was frustrated despite the Centre taking steps to address concerns related to students."Rahul Gandhi has completely turned mad. PM Narendra Modi has shown a magnanimous move by asking our education minister to resign. It's a great move because everybody thought otherwise, but PM Narendra Modi never thinks the unthinkable. So, he has done what was needed and has shown solidarity with the entire student community to show that he stands with them," Madhav said.The government will fight back with the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, listed for introduction in the Lok Sabha on Monday. The Bill, which was announced by Prime Minister Modi himself in a late-night video selfie, the first from the PM, proposes setting up fast-track courts in every state for paper leak cases and completion of investigations within two months.It also has provisions for enhanced punishment, including imprisonment of up to 10 years and fines up to Rs 50 lakh for individuals involved in paper leaks. Organised crimes related to paper leaks could attract fines of up to Rs 10 crore.Clearly, the government has a lot to showcase in terms of actions. Resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, PM Modi’s outreach to the students, new Bill with stringent provisions, fast track courts, task force under Nandan Nilekani, action against NTA officials, shifting out of the education secretary - these measures are going to power the government’s defence and offence. Also, the government will try to shift focus back on issues like Delimitation Bill to gain an upper hand over its political rivals.For the opposition, the July 20 police action against protesters is likely to be the rallying cry. The cops perhaps exceeded their brief in handling the protesters, and the opposition will go all out to ensure that the government does not get a breather, at least for now. The other key issue which the opposition would want to focus on to maintain pressure is the row Ram Mandir donation theft. Over to Parliament now for Round 2 of confrontation in monsoon session.
Article Summary: The stage has been set for the Round 2 of this confrontation. The government, armed with a slew of reform measures in the last few days, is all prepared to counter the opposition offensive. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has himself led this fightback. Opposition parties have signalled that they will keep the pressure going.

Article Title: CDSCO cancels 7 clinical trial ethics panels over serious violations
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has cancelled the registration of seven Ethics Committees across India overseeing clinical trials after inspections found serious violations of regulatory norms. The regulator said the committees failed to comply with the New Drugs and Clinical Trials (NDCT) Rules, 2019, Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines and other requirements, compromising their ability to carry out their responsibilities.The action covers Ethics Committees in Delhi, Pune, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata, which review and monitor clinical trials to protect the rights, safety and well-being of participants.The CDSCO said the committees were inspected as part of a risk-based compliance exercise to assess adherence to the NDCT Rules, 2019, Good Clinical Practice guidelines and quality management systems. The inspections identified significant deficiencies and major regulatory non-compliances in the functioning of the committees.According to the regulator, the registrations were cancelled only after completion of the regulatory process, including evaluation of inspection reports, review of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) responses, issuance of show-cause notices and personal hearings, wherever applicable.The seven committees whose registrations have been cancelled are Rational Independent Ethics Committee, New Delhi; Hurip Independent Bioethics Committee and Dr T K Pal Memorial Bio Ethics Committee, Kolkata; Ethiwell Ethics Committee and Ethos Ethics Committee, Navi Mumbai; Institutional Ethics Committee, Aatman Hospital, Ahmedabad; and Royal Pune Independent Ethics Committee, Pune.
Article Summary: The action covers Ethics Committees in Delhi, Pune, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata. The committees review and monitor clinical trials to protect the rights, safety and well-being of participants. The CDSCO said the committees were inspected as part of a risk-based compliance exercise.

Article Title: Infosys co-founder, Aadhaar architect: Who is Nandan Nilekani, set to lead high-powered exam reforms task force

Who is Nandan Nilekani

NEW DELHI: Continuing his announcements on examination reforms, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said the government has constituted a high-powered task force to be led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani "HIGH-POWERED TASK FORCE on examination reforms under the leadership of Shri Nandan Nilekani constituted," PM Modi said in a video message on X, a day after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical platform, called off its 37-day-long agitation following the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET (UG) question paper leak.Led by CJP, thousands of students had been on an indefinite sit-in in Delhi since June 21, demanding the resignation or removal of Pradhan and broader reforms in the education sector.Meanwhile, joining Nilekani on the task force are former Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) chairman S Somanath, former Intelligence Bureau (IB) director Tapan Deka, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary Anita Karwal, and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.Nilekani is the co-founder and chairman of Bengaluru-headquartered IT giant Infosys. He also served as the founding chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), the body that issues Aadhaar cards, with the rank of a Cabinet minister in the Congress-led central government from 2009 to 2014.In January 2023, he was appointed as the co-chair of the “G20 Task Force on Digital Public Infrastructure for Economic Transformation, Financial Inclusion, and Development.”Born in Bengaluru, Nilekani, 71, graduated from IIT Bombay in 1978. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian honour, in 2006. Time magazine named him among the world's 100 most influential people in 2006 and 2009, and included him in its 2024 list of the 100 Most Influential People in AI.Nilekani has also authored or co-authored three books.

Article Title: 'Govt-ordered probe an eyewash': Tripura Congress MLA demands judicial inquiry into DGP Anurag Dhankar's death
Article Text:
Tripura DGP Anurag Dhankar was found dead in state police headquarters on July 20

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Tripura Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman on Sunday reiterated the party's demand for a judicial probe into the death of state DGP Anurag Dhankar, who was found dead at the police headquarters in Agartala on July 20."From day one, we have been demanding a judicial probe by a sitting high court judge into the unnatural death of the DGP, keeping in mind the circumstances leading to the recovery of his body," he told a press conference at the Congress Bhavan in Agartala."The condition in which we saw his body at the morgue was as if he was in deep sleep, with no visible wounds that are generally found in such cases. We strongly believe that a team led by an SP-rank officer cannot clear the many doubts surrounding the incident.That is why we want a judicial inquiry into the unnatural death," Roy Barman added.A three-member team headed by West Tripura SP Namit Pathak has been constituted to investigate the matter.Roy Barman termed the Tripura government's decision to investigate the case through a three-member team as an "eyewash." He alleged that the "honest DGP was heckled over some issues days before his death."The Congress MLA also expressed disappointment over the Tripura high court not taking suo motu cognisance of Dhankar's death."The people of the state are also upset over the role of our high court. When the legislature, bureaucracy and media succumb, it is the judiciary that comes out and stands for the cause of people's rights. Unfortunately, we have not seen the high court take any suo motu cognisance in many incidents in the state since former Chief Justice Deepak Kumar Gupta's tenure ended," he said.Dhankar, a native of Uttar Pradesh's Baghpat, was a 1994-batch IPS officer of the Tripura cadre. He took over as the state's DGP in May 2025.The officer had led the CBI probe into the alleged Rs 13,000-crore Punjab National Bank fraud involving diamantaire Nirav Modi and the reinvestigation into the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.
Article Summary: Tripura DGP Anurag Dhankar was found dead at the police headquarters in Agartala on July 20. Tripura Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman reiterated the party's demand for a judicial probe into the death. A three-member team has been constituted to investigate the matter.
